1. A raindrop falls vertically from rest.
(a) State the initial acceleration of the raindrop. [1]
The graph shows how the speed of the raindrop varies with time $t$.
[Graph: speed against $t$/s from 0 to 5 s; speed rises from zero, curving, and levels off to a constant value after about 2–3 s]
(b) Explain, by reference to the vertical forces, how the raindrop reaches a constant speed. [3]
(c) During the first 3.0 s of motion, the raindrop falls a distance of 21 m and reaches a speed of $9.0\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. The mass of the raindrop is 34 mg. The temperature of the raindrop does not change.
(i) Determine the energy transferred to the air during the first 3.0 s of motion. State your answer to an appropriate number of significant figures. [3]
(ii) Describe the energy change that takes place for $t > 3.0$ s. [1]

2. A solar heating panel is placed on the roof of a house in order to heat water in a storage tank. The rest of the roof is covered with tiles.
(a) On a certain day, the intensity of the solar radiation that is incident perpendicular to the surface of the panel is $680\ \text{W m}^{-2}$.
The following data are available.
Mass of the water in the tank = 250 kg
Initial temperature of the water in the tank = 15 °C
Specific heat capacity of water = $4200\ \text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$
Overall efficiency of the heating system = 0.30
Albedo of the roof tiles = 0.20
Emissivity of the roof tiles = 0.97
(i) Determine the minimum area of the solar heating panel required to increase the temperature of all the water in the tank to 30 °C during a time of 1.0 hour. [3]
(ii) Estimate, in °C, the temperature of the roof tiles. [3]
(b) There is an air space above the water in the storage tank with an opening to the atmosphere. Assume that air behaves like an ideal gas.
[Diagram: storage tank filled with water, an air space above the water, and an opening at the top of the tank]
(i) State one way in which a real gas differs from an ideal gas. [1]
The air space is always at constant atmospheric pressure and constant volume, as the water level is kept constant. The air-space temperature and water temperature are the same.
(ii) The water is heated. Explain why the quantity of air in the storage tank decreases. [2]
(c) Another method of harnessing solar energy involves the use of photovoltaic cells.
Outline one advantage of the output of a photovoltaic cell compared to the output of a solar heating panel. [2]

3. A string of length 0.80 m is fixed at both ends. The diagram shows a standing wave formed on the string. P and Q are two particles on the string.
[Diagram: standing wave with three loops (1.5 wavelengths) between two fixed ends; P at an antinode in the first loop, Q in the third loop near a node]
(a) The variation with time $t$ of the displacement of particle P is shown.
[Graph: displacement of P against $t$/ms from 0 to 2.8 ms; cosine curve starting at a maximum, zero at about 0.7 ms, minimum at 1.4 ms, zero at about 2.1 ms, maximum at 2.8 ms]
(i) Draw, on the axes, a graph to show the variation with $t$ of the displacement of particle Q. [2]
(ii) Calculate the speed of waves on the string. [2]
(b) It is suggested that the speed $c$ of waves in the string is related to the tension force $T$ in the string according to the equation $T = ac^2$, where $a$ is a constant.
(i) Determine the fundamental SI unit for $a$. [2]
(ii) The tension force on the string is doubled. Describe the effect, if any, of this change on the frequency of the standing wave. [2]
(c) The standing wave on the string creates a travelling sound wave in the surrounding air.
(i) Outline one difference between a standing wave and a travelling wave. [1]
The sound wave is incident on a surface of water. The wave makes an angle of 30° with the normal to the surface.
[Diagram: sound wave direction incident from air onto an air–water boundary at 30° to the normal]
(ii) The speed of sound in air is $340\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and in water it is $1500\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Discuss whether the sound wave can enter the water. [2]

4. A mass is attached to one end of a rod and made to rotate with constant speed in a vertical circle.
[Diagram: rod pivoted at the centre of a dashed vertical circle, mass at the end of the horizontal rod, rotation clockwise]
(a) The scale diagram shows the weight $W$ of the mass at an instant when the rod is horizontal.
Draw, on the scale diagram, an arrow to represent the force exerted on the mass by the rod. [2]
[Scale diagram on a square grid: horizontal rod with the mass at its right end; weight $W$ drawn as a downward arrow two squares long]
(b) Explain why the magnitude of the force exerted on the mass by the rod is not constant. [3]

5. Resistor R is connected in a circuit with a cell that has internal resistance.
[Circuit: cell in series with ammeter A and resistor R; voltmeter V connected in parallel across the ammeter and R]
The ammeter and the voltmeter are ideal.
(a) State what is meant by an ideal voltmeter. [1]
(b) The resistance of R is $50.0\ \Omega$. The voltmeter reads 1.47 V.
(i) Calculate, in mA, the current in the resistor. [1]
Resistor R is replaced by another of resistance $10.0\ \Omega$. The ammeter now reads 139 mA.
(ii) Show that the internal resistance of the cell is about $0.7\ \Omega$. [2]
(iii) Calculate the emf of the cell. [2]
One of the connecting wires is placed in a magnetic field. The direction of the current in the wire is shown.
[Diagram: horizontal connecting wire between a N pole (above) and a S pole (below); current to the right]
(c) (i) Explain, by reference to charge carriers in the wire, how the magnetic force on the wire arises. [2]
(ii) Identify the direction of the magnetic force on the wire. [1]

6.text_clean:
6. (a) Outline, by reference to nuclear binding energy, why the mass of a nucleus is less than the sum of the masses of its constituent nucleons. [2]
Polonium-210 (Po-210) decays by alpha emission into lead-206 (Pb-206).
The following data are available.
Nuclear mass of Po-210 = 209.93676 u
Nuclear mass of Pb-206 = 205.92945 u
Mass of the alpha particle = 4.00151 u
(b) (i) Calculate, in MeV, the energy released in this decay. [2]
(ii) The polonium nucleus was stationary before the decay.
Show, by reference to the momentum of the particles, that the kinetic energy of the alpha particle is much greater than the kinetic energy of the lead nucleus. [3]
(iii) In the decay of polonium-210, alpha emissions can be accompanied by the emissions of gamma photons, all of the same wavelength of $1.54 \times 10^{-12}$ m.
Discuss how this observation provides evidence for discrete nuclear energy levels. [3]
(c) A sample contains 5.0 g of pure polonium-210. The decay constant of polonium-210 is $5.8 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. Lead-206 is stable.
Calculate the mass of lead-206 present in the sample after one year. [3]

7. A beam of coherent monochromatic light is incident normally on a single rectangular slit. The diffraction pattern is observed on a screen.
[Diagram: light source, single slit and screen; O on the screen directly opposite the slit, P above and Q below O]
O is the point on the screen directly opposite the slit. P and Q are the first minima on either side of the central fringe of the diffraction pattern.
(a) (i) The intensity of light at point O is $I_0$. The distance OP is $x$.
Sketch, on the axes, a graph to show the variation of the intensity of light with distance from point O on the screen. Your graph should cover the distance range from 0 to $2x$. [2]
[Blank axes: intensity (marked 0, $0.5I_0$, $I_0$) against distance (marked 0, $x$, $2x$)]
(ii) Early theories of light suggest that a geometrical shadow of the slit will be observed on the screen. Explain how the diffraction pattern formed on the screen provides evidence for the wave theory of light. [2]
(iii) The following data are available.
Wavelength of light = 590 nm
Distance between the slit and the screen = 2.4 m
Width of the slit = 0.10 mm
Calculate distance PQ. [2]
(b) The single slit is replaced by a double slit. The width of each slit in this arrangement is the same as the width of the single slit in (a).
Outline how the intensity variation observed between points P and Q will change. [2]
(c) The light source actually emits two wavelengths of light. The average wavelength is 590 nm and the difference between the two wavelengths is 0.60 nm.
A student attempts to resolve the wavelengths using a diffraction grating with 750 lines per mm. The incident beam is 2.0 mm wide.
Comment on whether this diffraction grating can resolve the wavelengths in the first-order spectrum. [3]

8. (a) The diagram shows field lines for an electrostatic field. X and Y are two points on the same field line.
[Diagram: three diverging electric field lines with arrows pointing to the left; X on the middle line at the left, Y on the same line further right]
Outline which of the two points has the larger electric potential. [2]
(b) A satellite is launched from the surface of Earth into a circular orbit.
The following data are given.
Mass of the satellite = $8.0 \times 10^{2}$ kg
Height of the orbit above the surface of Earth = $5.0 \times 10^{5}$ m
Mass of Earth = $6.0 \times 10^{24}$ kg
Radius of Earth = $6.4 \times 10^{6}$ m
(i) Show that the kinetic energy of the satellite in orbit is about $2 \times 10^{10}$ J. [2]
(ii) Determine the minimum energy required to launch the satellite. Ignore the original kinetic energy of the satellite due to Earth's rotation. [2]

9. A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance $1.5 \times 10^{-10}$ F is made from two metal plates separated by an air gap of 1.0 mm. The capacitor is initially charged to a potential difference of 24 V.
(a) Calculate the energy stored in the capacitor. [1]
The charged capacitor is disconnected from the voltage supply and the separation between the plates is increased to 4.0 mm.
(b) (i) Explain the change, if any, to the potential difference between the plates. [2]
(ii) Determine the work required to increase the separation of the plates. [2]
The capacitor is then discharged through a fixed resistor. The initial current in the resistor is $I_0$ and the time constant of the circuit is $\tau$.
(c) (i) Draw, on the axes, a graph to show the variation with time of the current in the resistor. [2]
[Blank axes: current (marked 0, $0.25I_0$, $0.5I_0$, $0.75I_0$, $I_0$) against time (marked 0, $\tau$, $2\tau$)]
(ii) A similar mathematical relationship can be used to model phenomena in other areas of physics.
State an example of such a phenomenon. [1]
(d) A diode bridge rectification circuit is often modified by adding a capacitor in parallel with the output (load) resistance.
Describe the reason for this modification. [2]

10. The Feynman diagram shows a delta baryon ($\Delta$) decaying into a neutron and particle X. The exchange particle involved in the decay is a gluon. Particle X has two constituent quarks.
[Feynman diagram: $\Delta$ (d d d) on the left becomes n (d d u) on the right; a gluon emitted from the third quark line produces a quark–antiquark pair forming particle X]
(a) (i) Identify the fundamental force responsible for the decay. [1]
(ii) Deduce, referring to one conservation law, that X is a quark-antiquark pair. [3]
(b) The energy released in the decay is of the order of $10^{8}$ eV.
Estimate, using the uncertainty principle, the mean lifetime of the delta baryon. [2]
